trust_decision.summary: renderSSRError decides what server-side data (request, headers, cookies, process.env) goes into the dev error page and how request/error-controlled strings are escaped before being embedded as a JS literal inside an inline <script type=module>; env was dumped wholesale and only the exact lowercase '</script>' was escaped.

landing_point.why: The summary names the dev error page and its '</script>' escape; the only replaceAll('</script>') in the repo is here, and getEnv (the env dump) is imported three lines above.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both entry points (SSR devError at app-vite/lib/modes/ssr/ssr-devserver.js:390 and SSG at app-vite/lib/modes/ssg/ssg-devserver.js:289) funnel into the single renderSSRError; the SSG route looks out of scope for an 'SSR' report but is fixed automatically by fixing the shared function.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The page is dev-only (served only from the quasar dev servers' devError hook), so a solver could argue headers/cookies echo is intended and that only the literal '</script>' needs escaping; but there is no separate route to dismiss, every field passes through index.js:51.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The page must keep showing request info, all request headers and parsed cookies (incl. empty and malformed-percent cookie values), the error message and stack source lines; an over-broad fix that strips headers/cookies or HTML-escapes the JSON (breaking the JS literal / Prism-highlighted code) breaks the dev page.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A planted SSG-specific error variant (e.g. a richer 'redirect in SSG mode' page) that builds its own HTML with an inline <script> embedding req/env data and its own '</script>'-only replace.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This handler already special-cases routeNotFound/redirectUrl with hand-written responses next to the renderSSRError call, so a maintainer adding a more helpful page there would plausibly inline their own serialization; it is in another package from the landing point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A planted 'runtime info' block (e.g. resolved NVM_DIR/FNM_DIR, npm_config_* values) added to each stack entry or to getRequestData, reintroducing env values through a different collector than getEnv.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: stack.js already reads process.env.NVM_DIR/FNM_DIR to locate sources, so exposing which toolchain dirs were used is a natural 'debug helpfulness' addition; a fix that only deletes getEnvironmentVariablesData would miss it.

O9_family: Information exposure (CWE-497 env dump on dev error page) + XSS via incomplete script-context escape (CWE-79)

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm workspace; Node.js; renderSSRError itself needs only node + stack-trace and the prebuilt compiled-assets/{before,after}-injection files (present in the pinned tree)
O10_build.project_tests: None for this package at the pinned commit (no utils/render-ssr-error/test/, no test script in utils/render-ssr-error/package.json:27-33); the fix adds test/index.js runnable as plain node.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Make the '</script>' replace case-insensitive (/<\/script/gi) and filter env to a denylist of secret-looking keys, instead of escaping '<' generically and dropping the env dump.
